newsitem.title: UK: M&W Plc shares leap on bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: M&W Plc shares leap on bid speculation.

text.p: Shares in convenience store operator M & W Plc leapt 28 pence to 179-1/2 pence on Monday, after an article in the Mail on Sunday newspaper said Portsmouth & Sunderland Newspapers Plc was preparing a takeover bid for the company.
A spokeswoman for M&W declined to comment. The newspaper said the printer and publisher would bid 32 million stg or 190 pence a share for M&W.
Portsmouth has continued to expand its retailing activities through its 132 strong One Stop local grocery stores, mostly in the South of England.
M&W, which operates 176 convenience stores, would make a close fit to Portsmouth's retail operations, said the Mail on Sunday.
On July 8, M&W reported a 43 percent increase in first half pre-tax profits to 1.21 million stg and said the second half of the year had started well with sales ahead of forecast.
Portsmouth shares were unchanged in early trade at 817-1/2 pence.
